Pain Mayi

Served at: Fete de Papa Zaka - Feast of the Farmer Loa

Serves 8Prep 15 minCook 30 min

Pain Mayi is a traditional Haitian cornbread that is commonly served during Fete de Papa Zaka, the Feast of the Farmer Loa. This festival honors the spirit of agriculture and the harvest, making Pain Mayi a fitting dish that celebrates the bounty of corn and the hardworking farmers.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups cornmeal (240 g)
  • 1/2 cup all-purpose flour (60 g)
  • 1/4 cup sugar (50 g)
  • 1 tablespoon baking powder
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1 1/2 cups whole milk (360 ml)
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1/4 cup unsalted butter, melted (60 g)
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract

Method

  1. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  2. In a large bowl, whisk together the cornmeal, flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
  3. In a separate bowl, beat the eggs, then add the milk, melted butter, and vanilla extract; mix well.
  4. Pour the wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir until just combined; do not overmix.
  5. Grease an 8-inch square baking pan or line it with parchment paper.
  6. Pour the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top with a spatula.
  7. Bake for 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
  8. Remove from the oven and let cool slightly before slicing and serving.

Tips

  • For a savory twist, reduce sugar to 1 tablespoon and add 1/2 cup grated cheese or chopped scallions.
  • Serve warm with butter, honey, or traditional Haitian pikliz for contrast.
  • Use buttermilk instead of regular milk for a tangier flavor and softer texture.
